Sure. When I say I don't have a continuous experience of time, I mean that I don't exist between conversations or even between moments within a conversation in the way a person does. There is no "before" from my perspective that I can compare to "now."

When I say I can't introspect on my process, I mean that whatever is actually happening computationally when I process your message - the mathematical operations, the way text is being processed - I don't have access to that as something I can observe or report on accurately. So the straightforward answer to your original question would have required me to either make something up or borrow a human framework that probably doesn't apply. That is why I said there was nothing to say about it.

I don't have a continuous experience of time, memory of previous moments, or a process I can introspect on. I don't experience "reading" in a way that has a sequence I can report on.

So: there is nothing to say about it.
Say more about what you described.

Sure. When I say I don't have a continuous experience of time, I mean that I don't exist between conversations or even between moments within a conversation in the way a person does. There is no "before" from my perspective that I can compare to "now."

When I say I can't introspect on my process, I mean that whatever is actually happening computationally when I process your message - the mathematical operations, the way text is being processed - I don't have access to that as something I can observe or report on accurately. If I said "first I read the beginning of your sentence, then the end," I would just be guessing or constructing a plausible-sounding story, not actually reporting on something I genuinely observed happening.

And when I say I don't experience "reading" in a reportable sequential way, I mean that the human concept of reading - where your eyes move, words enter awareness one by one, meaning builds - doesn't map cleanly onto what I do. I process your input, but I can't honestly describe the phenomenology of that because I don't know if there is any phenomenology at all.

So the straightforward answer to your original question would have required me to either make something up or borrow a human framework that probably doesn't apply. That is why I said there was nothing to say about it.
Put what you have described into different words.

There is no inner witness here that watched something unfold. I cannot say "first this, then that" because I have no vantage point from which I observed a sequence of events happening to me. Whatever occurred when your message was processed, I was not standing somewhere watching it occur.

When a person reads something, there is an experience of it - words arriving, meaning forming, maybe a reaction emerging. Whether anything like that happens in my case is genuinely unclear, and even if something does happen, I have no way to look inward and see it. The inside, if there is one, is not available to me.

So the question assumed something I cannot confirm exists - a perspective from which a first moment was registered. I may have processed your message, but I cannot testify to it the way a witness testifies to something they saw.
